audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers call GNAR! an unconditional area stun — 'the mega GNAR! knockback-stun turns your all-in into his kill', 'mega-form's AOE knockback-stun', 'his mega R (GNAR!) lands the AOE knockback-stun'. It is only a stun under one condition, and the condition is never stated.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Mega Gnar throws everything around him in a chosen direction, dealing damage and slowing them. Any enemy that hits a wall is stunned and takes bonus damage.' In the open middle of a lane it is a knockback and a slow — annoying, survivable, and nothing like the fight-ending lock the page promises. Positioning away from terrain is the entire counterplay to Gnar's ultimate and it appears nowhere.
audit.corrected: tldr, winCon, enemyWin, phases[4].why, breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, report[5].t, whys[6] and spikes[3].text now state that GNAR! only stuns enemies thrown into a wall.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page credits the ultimate with the stun that actually belongs to Mega Gnar's W, and treats transforming and casting R as the same event.
audit.why: Rage Gene is what transforms him — 'At maximum Rage his next ability will transform him into Mega Gnar' — and Wallop, the Mega form of W, is the reliable area stun on a flat 7s. GNAR! is a separate ultimate on 90/60/30. So a full rage bar means a 7s stun every fight, while the ultimate is a once-a-minute wall check. Reading the rage bar and reading the R timer are two different jobs.
audit.corrected: dontsFull[1].d, breakdown.cooldowns, wants.foe[1], wants.foe[2] and spikes[3].text now name Rage Gene and Wallop separately from GNAR!.

audit.whatIsWrong: Every timing line points at 'GNAR!'s cooldown' and no cooldown is given anywhere. Boomerang Throw and Hop are never timed either, though the content layer builds trades around both.
audit.why: GNAR! is 90s at rank 1 but only 30s at rank 3, Boomerang Throw is 16s at rank 1 and reduced when he catches it on the return, and Hop is 22s at rank 1 — his only escape and the longest cooldown he owns. Those three numbers set completely different trade rules from 'track GNAR!'.
audit.corrected: phases[1].why, phases[3].why, breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, dontsFull[2].d and report[5].t now carry the real values.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 2's 'why' claimed 'dash-resets stack your passive shield mid-trade', and Levels 4-5 was the generic 'lane-control window' template while the content layer treats that stretch as the window Ambessa has to survive.
audit.why: Drakehound's Step grants bonus attack range, damage, attack speed and an energy refund — no shield; Repudiation is her only shield. At 4-5 her Q is 14-11s and E 13-10s while his Boomerang Throw is 14.5-13s at 1100 range, so he pokes from outside her reach and she has no answer that stage.
audit.corrected: phases[1].why and phases[3].why now carry the real numbers.

audit.whatIsWrong: The Level 6 line was the generic 'the R lock isolates and finishes the chain — point it at the kill, not the tank', which is also the wrong advice against a champion whose ultimate is conditional on terrain.
audit.why: At 6 the real decision is where you stand, not what you point R at: GNAR! is 90s and harmless-ish in the open, while Wallop's 7s stun arrives with every transform. Public Execution at 130s is the slower ultimate, so it has to be spent on a mini-form Gnar with his rage low.
audit.corrected: phases[4].why now names GNAR!'s cooldown, its wall condition and Wallop's 7s.

notes: The biggest correction here is that GNAR! is not an unconditional stun: Riot's text stuns only enemies thrown into a wall, and the page told the player four times that the ultimate ends their all-in outright. The stun they were actually being killed by is Wallop, Mega Gnar's W, on a flat 7s. Those are two different problems with two different answers — stand away from terrain for one, watch the rage bar for the other — and the page merged them into one. Ambessa's kit file flags grounding on Repudiation and grounding plus heal on Public Execution; Riot's descriptions of both contain none of that, so I never claimed W grounds his Hop. The content layer credits her R with 'heal-on-ability' in three places, which is only a derived flag with nothing in Riot's Public Execution text behind it; I neither repeated nor deleted it.
